title: Chandni Bar Is Getting a Sequel. Tabu Returns. And Katrina Kaif Might Join Her.
excerpt: Twenty-five years after the National Award-winning original, the grittiest crime drama Bollywood ever made is coming back — with a casting rumour that could rewrite Katrina's entire career.
body:
Twenty-five years ago, a film about a bar dancer in Mumbai's underbelly won the National Award and turned Tabu into one of the most respected actresses in Indian cinema. Chandni Bar wasn't a hit in the traditional sense — it was something rarer. It was the kind of film people whispered about, passed around on pirated DVDs, wrote about in film school dissertations. It made you feel dirty for watching and ashamed for looking away. Now it's getting a sequel. And the casting rumour attached to it is the most exciting thing to come out of Bollywood this week.

According to a Filmfare exclusive, Katrina Kaif is in talks to star alongside Tabu in Chandni Bar 2. The film won't be directed by Madhur Bhandarkar, who helmed the 2001 original — instead, Ajay Bahl is at the wheel, a filmmaker whose work on Section 375 and Aadha has proven he knows how to navigate morally complex territory without flinching.

If this casting holds, it would represent two seismic things happening at once: a sequel to one of Bollywood's most uncompromising crime dramas, and the screen return of Katrina Kaif after nearly two years away.

Katrina's absence has been loud. Her last theatrical release was the Sriram Raghavan thriller Merry Christmas alongside Vijay Sethupathi in 2024. Since then, she stepped away from the public eye entirely after welcoming her son Vihaan Kaushal with husband Vicky Kaushal in November 2025. She's been photographed exactly as much as she wants to be — which is to say, barely at all. No airport looks. No pap walks. Just the occasional glimpse on Vicky's Instagram, and even those are rare.

The industry has been filling that silence with speculation. Earlier this week, reports surfaced claiming Katrina was reading scripts and eyeing OTT projects for a 2027 return. Her team shut those reports down with startling bluntness: "There is absolutely no truth to the claims being made about Katrina Kaif's future acting plans. The report is based entirely on speculation and misinformation."

But the Filmfare report about Chandni Bar 2 is a different animal. It comes from what the outlet describes as a well-placed source, and it's specific: Katrina and Tabu, together, in a film rooted in Mumbai's red-light district and crime ecosystem. No OTT. No limited series. A theatrical feature that trades on grit, not gloss.

The original Chandni Bar is a gut punch of a film even today. Tabu played Mumtaz, a naive village girl forced into bar dancing in Mumbai, who watches her world collapse around her as her children are pulled into the same underworld she tried to escape. It won Bhandarkar the National Award for Best Director and Tabu the National Award for Best Actress. The film made no compromises. It didn't ask you to like its characters. It asked you to see them.

A sequel 25 years later, in a city that has changed dramatically but whose power structures haven't budged, feels both overdue and necessary. The original film's dance bars have been the subject of Supreme Court battles, political campaigns, and social upheaval since 2001. There's a world of story there.

What makes the Katrina angle electrifying is the departure it represents. This is an actress whose filmography is built on spectacle — Ek Tha Tiger, Dhoom 3, Tiger Zinda Hai, Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara. She's one of the biggest commercial stars of her generation, and she's never done anything remotely like what Chandni Bar demands. If she takes this role, it won't just be a comeback. It'll be a reinvention.

For the diaspora, the prospect of Tabu and Katrina sharing the screen in a film that takes Mumbai's margins seriously is the kind of project you mark on the calendar. The original Chandni Bar streams on JioCinema — if you haven't seen it, this is your excuse. And if you have, you already know why a sequel with this cast is worth paying attention to.

The makers haven't released an official cast list yet, and Filmfare notes they couldn't get a comment from director Ajay Bahl. But the prospect alone — Tabu returning to a role that defined her career, Katrina stepping into territory that could redefine hers — is the most compelling casting conversation Bollywood has had in months.

We'll be watching. Closely.
